A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same auction mechanism and synthetic advertising study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable; v2's Electronic Companion can be matched to v4's Appendices A-C.

before.justification: Section 6 and EC.3 report original LLM experiments using 50 synthetic queries, two advertisers per query, and 25 seeds, with reward, revenue, utility, and generated-output results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original experiments over 1,250 instances, including advertiser outcomes and an additional analysis of returned replies under the reference model.

M1.justification: MOSAIC names the existing mechanism. Algorithm 1 retains candidate generation and softmax selection using rewards and likelihood ratios; the payment rule and zero-bid offset also remain unchanged. The generic generation-model notation replaces an explicitly contextual notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic online-advertising coverage with 50 queries and two fictitious advertisers per query. The added usefulness analysis evaluates the existing setting; the musical-instrument example already appears in v2.

E2.justification: The reference-generated baseline and payments with and without offsets are retained. The new usefulness plot reuses direct reference-model sampling, already used as the optimal-model proxy in v2 Figure 1a. Newly cited auction methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds evaluation using returned-reply log probability under the reference LLM as a usefulness proxy. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged, including Llama-2-7b-chat-hf, tau = 1, temperature 0.8, and top-p 0.95.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds analysis of how candidate count affects the user-usefulness proxy and its gap to reference sampling. The existing context and payment-offset comparisons, regression analyses, and qualitative output example are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions document 25 seeds per query, 1,250 runs, and 95% confidence intervals, alongside the same correlation and regression reporting. No new empirical replication or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: New Figure 3 reports that context-aware reply likelihood under the reference model increases with candidate count but remains below direct reference sampling. Existing convergence, reward, revenue, and payment results match, including R-squared values 0.61 and 0.12 in v2 Figure EC.2 and v4 Figure 5.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 defines an importance-sampling estimator and derives its expectation and variance in Equations (7)-(10), adding formal analysis of proposal-distribution choice and candidate count. This substantially extends the mathematical treatment beyond v2's retained convergence and payment proofs.

C1.justification: The central optimality, strategyproofness, welfare-alignment, and API-access claims remain. However, v4 explicitly restricts empirical ex-ante individual-rationality statements in the introduction and Remark 2 to the tested instance distribution, where v2 states them more generally.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations concerning competition in thin markets, the baseline's declining advertiser rewards, and the reference-weight trade-off underlying the usefulness gap. It also identifies adaptive candidate budgets and formal context design as future directions.

D1.justification: The detailed prompts, reward normalization, sampling parameters, hardware, operating system, Python version, and promised future release of code and synthetic instances are retained. Compute information moves from EC.3.2 into C.1 without substantive revision.

R1.justification: v4 adds a focused comparison with Hajiaghayi et al.'s RAG auction, distinguishing scalar bids from misreportable full LLMs, and cites Werner et al., Rockafellar, and additional application context. It shortens the Dubey comparison and removes one criticism of Duetting et al.; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution narrative, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Challenges are integrated into the contributions, MOSAIC and advertiser terminology are adopted throughout, appendix subsections are reorganized, and the author block changes.

P2.justification: Typography, spacing, and figure placement are substantially reformatted. Revenue becomes a standalone figure, the correlation plot moves to Appendix Figure 7, and the usefulness Figure 3 is added. The separate utility panel disappears, but its results remain in the appendix. New Figure 3 incorrectly captions likelihood as revenue.

improvement.justification: The user-likelihood analysis and explicit trade-off discussion address a limited gap in v2's evaluation, while revised exposition and qualified IR claims improve clarity and precision. The gains are limited: usefulness remains a likelihood proxy, the new importance-sampling calculation concerns an auxiliary estimator rather than directly bounding Algorithm 1, and Figure 3 has an incorrect revenue caption.
